projects.title: PINTER AI Agent Platform
projects.description: Internal AI agent platform for Pupuk Indonesia Holding Company. Teams build Google ADK agent graphs on a visual canvas, connect MCP tools, and chat through virtual models that route each query with the TypeSafe Jev smart router.
projects.summary: PINTER is the internal AI agent platform of Pupuk Indonesia Holding Company, built on FastAPI, Google ADK, and React 19. I have worked on it since January 2026, through the move from CrewAI to ADK and the later refactor. My main work is the async SQLAlchemy backend, the agent runtime behind the canvas (HITL, conditional agents, sub-agents), prompt extraction defense, RBAC and sharing, CI speed, and the TypeSafe Jev smart router.

fiveWOneH.who: Aditya Vahlevy Nugraha as the second-largest contributor in a team of two to four engineers. Original repositories: 331 of 865 backend and 212 of 717 frontend commits. Refactor repositories: 247 of 498 backend and 236 of 457 frontend commits. About 40% of 2,500+ commits overall.
fiveWOneH.what: An agent platform with a visual ADK graph builder, MCP tool servers, virtual models (combos, round-robin, smart router), role-based sharing, and chat with an inline execution trace.
fiveWOneH.when: January 2026 to now. Original repositories until early September 2026, then the refactor repositories.
fiveWOneH.where: Internal deployment at Pupuk Indonesia Holding Company, with sign-in through the IDENTIK SSO.
fiveWOneH.why: Let business teams build and run agents without code, safely, and send each query to a model that fits it instead of one fixed model.
fiveWOneH.how: FastAPI, Google ADK, and async SQLAlchemy on the backend, React 19 with React Flow and TanStack on the frontend, GitLab CI on pre-baked images, and an httpx client for the TypeSafe Jev System One endpoint.

problemChangeResult.problem: The first backend used raw psycopg2 SQL and CrewAI-era routes, which made schema changes risky.
problemChangeResult.change: Moved to async SQLAlchemy with Alembic, new /api/v2 routes with execution tracing and per-user quotas, and wrote a v1 to v2 migration guide so old routes kept working (ad20a97).
problemChangeResult.result: Schema changes go through Alembic revisions. Old routes stayed available during the switch.

problemChangeResult.problem: Agents could leak their system prompt when users asked for it (CWE-1427).
problemChangeResult.change: Built a two-layer prompt guard: an input filter that refuses extraction attempts before the model call, and an output filter that redacts leaked instruction sections before streaming or storage (f737fd2).
problemChangeResult.result: Extraction attempts get a safe refusal, and leaked sections never reach the client or the database. Attack success rate: Not measured.

problemChangeResult.problem: Backend lint and audit jobs reinstalled their tools on every pipeline.
problemChangeResult.change: Pre-baked a dependency image tagged by the requirements hash and moved the verify jobs onto it, with a drift guard between the image and its checks (c080472, 5d7a69b, e8a9302).
problemChangeResult.result: Measured on MR 341: each job went from 6m11s to 7m28s down to 1m24s cold and 13s warm.

problemChangeResult.problem: Every agent call went to one fixed model, whatever the query.
problemChangeResult.change: Added a smart router virtual model. The TypeSafe Jev client scores the query against route criteria. The router picks a route when confidence passes a threshold (default 0.65) and falls back to a general model otherwise.
problemChangeResult.result: Routing logic and threshold covered by frontend tests in virtual-models.test.ts. List-price estimate: about 34% cheaper than sending everything to the strongest model. Real cost and latency: Not measured.

keyDecisions.decision: Guard the prompt on both sides
keyDecisions.explanation: The input filter stops obvious extraction attempts before a model call is paid for. The output filter catches what slips through. A fixed clause in every system prompt adds a third check (modules/adk/prompt_guard.py).

The router calls the TypeSafe Jev System One endpoint through one pooled httpx client instead of asking a general LLM to triage. Trade-off: one more external dependency on the request path (modules/agents/runtime/typesafe_client.py).
A route is used only above a configurable threshold, default 0.65. Below it the request goes to a fallback model, so a weak classification never blocks chat (modules/agents/virtual_models.py).

keyDecisions.decision: Dependency image keyed by the lockfile
keyDecisions.explanation: The image tag is the requirements hash, so its layer digest stays stable and the registry can reuse it. Trade-off: the image and the CI checks must list the same tools, so a test guards that (c080472, e8a9302).

projects.caseStudy: PINTER is the internal AI agent platform of Pupuk Indonesia Holding Company. Teams build agents on a React Flow canvas that maps to Google ADK graphs: single LLM agents, sequential, parallel, and loop agents. Agents can call MCP tool servers over stdio, SSE, or streamable HTTP. I joined the work in January 2026, when the platform still ran on CrewAI and raw SQL. I migrated the agent framework from CrewAI to Google ADK, refactored the frontend and backend, and moved the backend to async SQLAlchemy and Alembic behind new routes, and kept the old ones alive through a written migration guide. On the runtime side I added human-in-the-loop and conditional agents, and sub-agents that can be toggled, promoted, and tested alone on the canvas. Agents could be asked to reveal their system prompt, so I built a guard that refuses those requests before the model call and redacts leaked instructions before anything is streamed or saved. I built the L1 to L4 access levels and sharing by grant or code, and later closed P0 bypasses by moving every route to exact permission checks. Backend CI reinstalled its tools on every run, so I pre-baked a dependency image. Lint and audit jobs went from about 7 minutes to 13 seconds once warm. After the refactor in September 2026, I added a smart router as a new virtual model type. The backend asks the TypeSafe Jev System One endpoint for a confidence score per route. Above the threshold, default 0.65, the router uses the matching model. Below it, the request goes to a fallback model. The decision shows in the chat trace. I also added Jev guardrail middleware and IDENTIK SSO with AES-256-GCM encrypted assertions. Latency and cost effects of routing are not measured yet.
details: Moved the backend from raw psycopg2 to async SQLAlchemy with Alembic, new /api/v2 routes, execution tracing, and per-user quotas, with a v1 to v2 migration guide.
Added human-in-the-loop and conditional agents, and split the executor into runner and persister.
Built canvas sub-agent support: toggle, promotion with template diffing, single sub-agent testing, and transfer tracing over SSE.
Built a two-layer guard against system prompt extraction (CWE-1427) with input refusal and output redaction.
Built L1 to L4 RBAC, marketplace approvals, access mapping, and sharing by grant or redeemable code, with a 1,200-line test suite. Closed P0 RBAC bypasses.
Pre-baked the CI dependency image. Lint and audit jobs dropped from 6 to 7 minutes to 1m24s cold and 13s warm.
Built the TypeSafe Jev client with a pooled httpx connection and the smart router virtual model with confidence threshold and fallback.
Streamed routing decisions and the active model to chat and rendered them in the inline trace.
Added IDENTIK SSO encrypted assertions (AES-256-GCM with an HKDF-derived key) and an external user ID backfill.
Added System One Jev guardrail middleware, workspace guardrail policies, and a guardrail settings panel.
projects.rationale: Internal tool that lets teams at Pupuk Indonesia Holding Company build AI agents without code and route each query to a suitable model.
technicalChallenges: Kept old routes working while the backend moved to a new ORM and schema, through deprecated shims and a written migration path.
Redacted leaked system prompt sections from model output before streaming or storage, without blocking normal questions about the agent's role.
Kept routing safe when the classifier is unsure: below the confidence threshold the request falls back to a general model instead of failing.
Kept the CI image and its checks in sync with a guard test that fails when a tool is added to one and not the other (e8a9302).

projects.title: AeGIS Module Atlas
projects.description: Fertilizer demand planning map for Pupuk Indonesia. Planners edit dosage and planting stage inputs and see demand recalculated in the browser, next to the GeoMind AI assistant.
projects.summary: Atlas is the fertilizer demand planning app inside the AeGIS monorepo at Pupuk Indonesia. I scaffolded its first version, moved the map to OpenLayers, and built the client-side demand formula engine with 52 unit tests. On the Go backend I made the overview queries date-bounded and coalesced.

fiveWOneH.who: Aditya Vahlevy Nugraha, as one of three engineers on AeGIS. Aditya authored 349 frontend commits and 59 backend commits. The monorepo, Go backend, Halo, and Tango apps were built by colleagues.
fiveWOneH.what: The Atlas app: demand map, overview dashboard, formula editor, GeoMind assistant workspace, and data playground.
fiveWOneH.where: Internal planning tool at Pupuk Indonesia Holding Company.
fiveWOneH.why: Planners recalculated fertilizer demand by hand when dosage or land assumptions changed.
fiveWOneH.how: React 19 and OpenLayers in a Bun and Turborepo monorepo, with a Go Fiber v3 backend.

problemChangeResult.result: 52 unit tests pass with 86 assertions (bun test, formula-calc.test.ts). Planner time saved: Not measured.

projects.caseStudy: Atlas is the fertilizer demand planning app in the AeGIS monorepo at Pupuk Indonesia Holding Company. Planners combine planting stages, dosage, and land area to estimate demand per region. When an assumption changed, they recalculated by hand. I scaffolded the first version of the app and later moved its map from MapLibre to OpenLayers. The main piece is a formula engine that runs in the browser. It allocates demand across planting stages, applies land area overrides, and computes the difference from the baseline. A formula editor store tracks each change. Because the engine runs client-side, the numbers update on each edit without a server call. To keep the math honest, the engine has 52 unit tests covering stage allocation, overrides, and float tolerance. On the Go backend, I changed the overview queries from EXTRACT on year and month to date ranges, coalesced identical in-flight requests, and added a short cache. I also built the GeoMind workspace, where the AI assistant and the map share filters both ways. The monorepo, the Go service framework, and the Halo and Tango apps are my colleagues' work.
details: Scaffolded the first version of the Atlas app (then geodash) in the AeGIS frontend monorepo.
Migrated the map canvas from MapLibre GL to OpenLayers.
Built a client-side fertilizer demand formula engine with stage allocation, land overrides, and demand deltas, covered by 52 unit tests.
Built a formula editor store with derived change tracking.
Built the GeoMind assistant workspace with two-way sync between chat and map filters, and fixed double-encoded stream payloads.
Replaced EXTRACT-based overview filters with month date bounds, added in-flight request coalescing and a 60 second cache, and added 5 headline insights.
Added a Graphic Walker playground for exploring demand data.
Fixed backend panics and socket exhaustion in the Atlas service.
Built a tile proxy for the Martin tile server with HMAC token auth, header forwarding, path traversal guard, and a 1MB response cap. Removed it later with other unused routes.
projects.rationale: Planning tool that helps Pupuk Indonesia estimate fertilizer demand per region and see the effect of changed assumptions right away.
technicalChallenges: Kept floating point results stable across stage redistribution, with tolerance checks in the formula tests.
Kept chat filters and map filters in sync both ways in the GeoMind workspace without loops (2ce3701).
Stopped duplicate overview queries under concurrent load with in-flight coalescing (f123900).
Moved SNM feature deduplication to a Web Worker so tile processing does not block the main thread (snm-worker.ts).

projects.title: NEXUS (Arca, Delta & Vista)
projects.description: Logistics platform for Pupuk Indonesia's fertilizer distribution. Delta manages carrier contracts and freight tariffs, Vista simulates routes on a Neo4j graph, and Arca monitors warehouse and kiosk stock.
projects.summary: NEXUS is the logistics platform for fertilizer distribution at Pupuk Indonesia Holding Company. I am the main author: 197 of 262 backend commits and 327 of 335 frontend commits. I built the multi-entry frontend, the Delta contract and tariff tools including BBM fuel freight simulation, and the route optimizer service, and I ported Arca into the platform.

fiveWOneH.who: Aditya Vahlevy Nugraha as main author. Colleagues wrote the original Neo4j Cypher scripts and part of Arca.
fiveWOneH.what: Three modules on one platform: Delta (contracts, tariffs, BBM freight adjustment), Vista (route simulation on a map), and Arca (warehouse and kiosk stock monitoring).
fiveWOneH.where: Internal logistics tool at Pupuk Indonesia Holding Company.
fiveWOneH.why: Freight tariffs, contracts, and routes lived in spreadsheets, and route costs were worked out by hand.
fiveWOneH.how: React 19 with Rsbuild multi-entry builds, FastAPI with async SQLAlchemy on PostgreSQL, Neo4j for the route graph, and openpyxl for Excel import.

problemChangeResult.problem: Tariffs came from spreadsheets, and a bad import could overwrite existing rates.
problemChangeResult.change: Built a tariff Excel import with a preview step and a conflict resolution dialog before commit (tarif_routes.py, TariffConflictModal.tsx).
problemChangeResult.result: Conflicts are shown before data is written. Error rate change: Not measured.

problemChangeResult.problem: Fuel (BBM) price changes had to be applied to freight tariffs by hand.
problemChangeResult.change: Built BBM parameter alignment and freight adjustment simulation in Delta (c3d3f61, a32852d).
problemChangeResult.result: Freight impact of a BBM change can be simulated before applying it. Time saved: Not measured.

problemChangeResult.problem: Each module needed its own dev setup, and Delta pulled in Neo4j it did not use.
problemChangeResult.change: Built Rsbuild multi-entry builds selected by APP_MODULE and an enable_neo4j startup flag for standalone backends.
problemChangeResult.result: Delta, Vista, Arca, and the shell build and run on their own. Build time: Not measured.

contributions: Built the multi-entry frontend (shell, Delta, Vista, Arca) and restructured both repositories into symmetric monorepos (07cea38, a91a980).
Built BBM fuel parameter alignment and freight adjustment simulation (c3d3f61, a32852d).
Added configurable contract expiry alert thresholds (925aee5).
Ported the Arca stock dashboard and added the global auth module, with another engineer contributing (dab13dc).
Built the route optimizer service on top of the Neo4j graph and extended the Cypher route search.
Moved UI primitives into a shared package and added the pytest suite (93c92fc, c8ba061).

Build time per module before and after the multi-entry setup.

keyDecisions.explanation: Rsbuild picks the entry from APP_MODULE, so each module runs alone in development and ships together in the shell. Trade-off: shared code must stay in the shared package (rsbuild.config.ts, 93c92fc).
create_app takes enable_neo4j, so Delta and Arca start without a graph database. Only Vista and the shell connect to Neo4j (packages/core/factory.py).
The Excel import runs a preview and asks the user to resolve conflicts before commit, so existing tariffs are never overwritten silently (packages/delta/routes/tarif_routes.py).

projects.caseStudy: NEXUS supports fertilizer distribution logistics at Pupuk Indonesia Holding Company. Before it, freight tariffs, carrier contracts, and route costs lived in spreadsheets. I am the main author of both repositories. The platform has three modules. Delta holds carrier contracts and freight tariffs. Tariffs come in from Excel through a preview step that shows conflicts before anything is written. When fuel (BBM) prices change, Delta can simulate the freight adjustment before it is applied. Contract expiry alerts have configurable warning and critical thresholds. Vista draws routes on an OpenLayers map and uses a route optimizer service over a Neo4j graph. Colleagues wrote the original Cypher scripts, and I extended the route search. Arca monitors warehouse and kiosk stock. I ported it from an earlier stock dashboard together with another engineer. All modules live in one frontend repository. Rsbuild picks the entry from APP_MODULE, so each module runs alone during development. On the backend, Delta and Arca start without Neo4j through a startup flag. Performance and savings are not measured yet.
details: Built Rsbuild multi-entry builds selected by APP_MODULE for the shell, Delta, Vista, and Arca.
Restructured frontend and backend into symmetric monorepos with a shared UI package.
Built tariff Excel import with preview and conflict resolution, using openpyxl on the backend and exceljs for export.
Built BBM fuel parameter alignment and freight adjustment simulation.
Added configurable contract expiry alert thresholds.
Built the route optimizer service over the Neo4j route graph and drew routes on an OpenLayers map in Vista.
Added an enable_neo4j startup flag so standalone Delta and Arca run without a graph database.
Ported the Arca warehouse and kiosk stock dashboard and added the global auth module, with another engineer.
Added the backend pytest suite and Arca route tests.
projects.rationale: Internal logistics tool that replaces spreadsheets for freight tariffs, contracts, and route costs at Pupuk Indonesia Holding Company.
technicalChallenges: Kept modules independent in one repository: each runs alone in development and they ship together in the shell build.
Detected tariff conflicts during Excel import and let users resolve them before commit.
Fixed CORS for credentialed requests by echoing the exact origin with allow_origin_regex (bf69b4b).
Fixed Docker builds by copying workspace manifests before bun install (495d080).

projects.title: SAM3 Dashboard & Playground
projects.description: An interactive full-stack dashboard for Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3), providing a complete pipeline for image segmentation, model fine-tuning, data labeling, and performance evaluation on geospatial/satellite imagery.
details: Built a complete SAM3 environment with Dashboard (system health), Inference (text/box/point prompts), Training (fine-tuning with TensorBoard), and Evaluation (IoU metrics).
Implemented a 3-phase Data Engine pipeline: Batch Processing → Human Verification (accept/reject/flag) → Polygon Correction with Fabric.js editor.
Developed a Polygon Editor with vertex editing, simplification, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts (V/E/H/D modes), undo/redo, and zoom/pan controls.
Created Dataset management for uploading ZIP datasets (COCO format), converting image+mask folders, and validating local paths.
Exports COCO-format datasets with RLE encoding ready for SAM3 training.
Backend built with FastAPI, SQLAlchemy (SQLite), and OpenCV for image processing.
Frontend built with Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, TailwindCSS v4, DaisyUI v5, Fabric.js, and Chart.js.
Supports TIFF, PNG, JPG formats with real-time mask visualization overlays.

projects.title: Land Delineation Training
projects.description: Deep learning model training pipeline for delineating land from satellite imagery. Features preprocessing, BsiNet model implementation, and custom loss functions.
details: Developed a deep learning pipeline for land delineation using BsiNet architecture.
Implemented preprocessing modules using GDAL for satellite imagery (GeoTIFF) handling, including normalization, mask binarization, and resampling.
Created a custom PyTorch dataset loader handling images, masks, contours, and distance maps.
Defined and implemented custom loss functions including Dice Loss, Focal Loss, and a combined LossBsiNet.
Set up a training loop with TensorBoard logging for monitoring model performance.
Built a testing script to generate binary masks from model predictions and save them as GeoTIFFs.

Collected and preprocessed data from East and West Java (2020-2021).
Applied classical ML models (RF, XGBoost, LightGBM) and deep learning models (LSTM, GRU).
Implemented transfer learning for the Lampung region to improve prediction accuracy.
Achieved region-specific yield predictions with improved accuracy.
Gained skills in integrating geospatial data with ML/DL models and remote sensing analysis.
